group.passage:
In April 2003, scientists announced that they had finished reading the human genome, the roughly 3 billion chemical “letters” that make up our DNA. The Human Genome Project had taken thirteen years and brought together researchers from six countries. Most of the DNA they read came from anonymous volunteers, about 70 percent of it from a single person. Producing that first sequence is thought to have cost between $500 million and $1 billion, while the project as a whole, which also developed new tools and studied other living things, cost roughly $3 billion. Even then, the job was not quite complete: the 2003 version covered about 92 percent of the genome and still had hundreds of gaps, which were not filled until 2022.
Since then, the cost of reading a genome has collapsed. The National Human Genome Research Institute in the United States has tracked what the research centers it funds spend to sequence a genome, and the chart below shows the result. In 2002, the cost was about $61 million. It fell steadily for several years, and then, in 2008, the centers replaced their older machines with a new generation of machines, and the figure began to drop far more quickly. By 2022, sequencing a genome cost only about $525. That is a drop of more than 100,000 times in just twenty years.
These figures need to be read with some care. They include staff, equipment, and chemicals, but not the later work of making sense of the data. Companies also count their costs in different ways, so the price a patient is charged may be quite different from the cost reported here.
Cheaper sequencing has already begun to change medicine. Doctors now use genetic information to help choose cancer treatments, to decide which drugs suit a patient, and to identify rare diseases that had gone undiagnosed. Still, it is often estimated that a new medical discovery takes 17 years, on average, to become part of everyday care. Being able to read a genome for a few hundred dollars is a remarkable step, but understanding what it says, and using that knowledge wisely, remains the harder task.

figures.description: 折線圖。橫軸是年份（2002 到 2022，每兩年一個點），縱軸是定序一個人類基因體的成本（美元，未經通膨調整），只有一條線。數值依序是 2002 年 61,448,420、2004 年 18,519,312、2006 年 10,474,556、2008 年 342,502、2010 年 29,092、2012 年 5,901、2014 年 4,008、2016 年 1,176、2018 年 1,232、2020 年 512、2022 年 525。縱軸是一般（非對數）刻度，2008 年以後的點幾乎都貼在底部。資料來源：Our World in Data（原始資料：美國國家人類基因體研究所）。

chart.note: The vertical scale is ordinary (not logarithmic), so the values from 2008 onward lie very close to the bottom of the chart; see the data table for exact figures. Costs are not adjusted for inflation.

questions.stem: According to the chart, which of the following is true?

options.A: The cost went down in every two-year period shown.
options.B: The cost fell by the largest amount of money between 2008 and 2010.
options.C: By 2010, the cost was less than one-thousandth of what it had been in 2002.
options.D: The cost fell faster between 2008 and 2010 than between 2006 and 2008.

questions.stem: Why does the author point out that the figures leave out the work of making sense of the data?

options.A: To warn that the full cost of using a genome may be higher than the chart shows.
options.B: To explain why the cost went up again in some years after 2016.
options.C: To suggest that the institute kept careless records of its spending.
options.D: To argue that companies charge patients too much for sequencing.

questions.stem: What does the author suggest in the last paragraph?

options.A: Doctors will soon stop using genetic information in cancer care.
options.B: Cheap sequencing alone will not quickly transform ordinary medical care.
options.C: The cost of reading a genome is likely to rise sharply again.
options.D: Most rare diseases can now be cured by reading a patient’s genome.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the Human Genome Project?

options.A: It spent about $3 billion on producing the first human genome sequence.
options.B: It produced the first truly complete copy of the human genome.
options.C: All of the DNA it read came from a single volunteer.
options.D: It announced it had finished even though parts of the genome were still missing.

option_notes_zh.B: 金額降最多的是 2002→2004 年（約少了 4,290 萬美元）；2008→2010 年只少了約 31 萬美元。文中提到 2008 年換新機器，容易讓人誤以為那兩年降最多。

1.strategy_zh: 一般刻度的折線圖上，數值很小的點會擠在底部，看起來像「沒有變化」或「一直下降」，一定要打開資料表核對數字。比較「降了多少錢」和「降為幾分之一」是兩件不同的事。
hints: 2002 年與 2010 年的成本各是多少？
61,448,420 的千分之一大約是多少？

2.explanation_zh: 第三段一開始就提醒這些數字要小心解讀：它們包含人力、設備和化學藥劑，但不包含後續解讀資料的工作。指出「沒算進去的部分」，用意是提醒讀者：真正把基因體用在醫療上的完整花費，可能比圖表上的數字高，所以選 A。
evidence: These figures need to be read with some care.
They include staff, equipment, and chemicals, but not the later work of making sense of the data.

option_notes_zh.C: 與原文不符：作者沒有說研究所的紀錄有錯，只是說明這些數字涵蓋的範圍。
option_notes_zh.D: 過度推論：文中只說公司收的價格可能和這裡的成本「很不一樣」，可能較高也可能較低，並沒有說收費太高。

hints: 第三段的第一句提醒讀者什麼？

evidence: Still, it is often estimated that a new medical discovery takes 17 years, on average, to become part of everyday care.
Being able to read a genome for a few hundred dollars is a remarkable step, but understanding what it says, and using that knowledge wisely, remains the harder task.

3.strategy_zh: 推論作者的看法，要特別注意轉折詞（Still、but）後面的內容，那通常是作者真正想強調的重點。
hints: 最後一段的 Still 前後在說什麼？
一項新發現平均要多久才會成為日常醫療？

option_notes_zh.B: 細節錯置：2003 年的版本仍有缺口，真正完整的序列要到 2022 年才完成。
option_notes_zh.C: 過度概括：約 70% 的 DNA 來自同一個人，其餘來自其他匿名志願者。

A: Producing that first sequence is thought to have cost between $500 million and $1 billion, while the project as a whole, which also developed new tools and studied other living things, cost roughly $3 billion.
B: Even then, the job was not quite complete: the 2003 version covered about 92 percent of the genome and still had hundreds of gaps, which were not filled until 2022.

4.strategy_zh: 細節題的誘答常把同一段裡的數字或對象換位置（整個計畫 vs. 第一份序列、大部分 vs. 全部、宣布完成 vs. 真正完整），要逐字對回原文。
hints: 2003 年的版本涵蓋了多少比例的基因體？
約 30 億美元是誰的花費？第一份序列花了多少？
DNA 全部來自一個人嗎？

translation_zh.text:
2003 年 4 月，科學家宣布已經讀完人類基因體，也就是構成我們 DNA 的約 30 億個化學「字母」。人類基因體計畫歷時十三年，集合了來自六個國家的研究人員。他們讀取的 DNA 大多來自匿名志願者，其中約 70% 來自同一個人。據估計，產生這第一份序列就花了 5 億到 10 億美元；而整個計畫（也開發新工具、研究其他生物）大約花了 30 億美元。即使如此，工作還沒有完全完成：2003 年的版本約涵蓋基因體的 92%，仍有數百個缺口，直到 2022 年才補齊。
從那時起，讀取一個基因體的成本便大幅崩落。美國國家人類基因體研究所持續記錄它資助的研究中心定序一個基因體要花多少錢，下圖就是結果。2002 年，成本約 6,100 萬美元。之後幾年穩定下降；到了 2008 年，這些中心把舊機器換成新一代的機器，數字開始下降得快得多。到了 2022 年，定序一個基因體只要約 525 美元。短短二十年間，成本降為原來的十萬分之一以下。
這些數字需要謹慎解讀。它們包含人力、設備和化學藥劑，但不包含後續解讀資料的工作。各公司計算成本的方式也不一樣，所以病人被收取的價格，可能和這裡記錄的成本相差很多。
比較便宜的定序已經開始改變醫療。醫生現在用基因資訊來幫忙選擇癌症療法、判斷哪些藥適合病人，並找出原本沒被診斷出來的罕見疾病。不過，一般估計一項新的醫學發現平均要 17 年，才會成為日常醫療的一部分。能用幾百美元讀取一個基因體是很了不起的一步，但讀懂它的內容並明智地運用這些知識，仍是更困難的工作。
【圖】折線圖：定序一個人類基因體的成本（美元，未經通膨調整），2002 年 61,448,420、2004 年 18,519,312、2006 年 10,474,556、2008 年 342,502、2010 年 29,092、2012 年 5,901、2014 年 4,008、2016 年 1,176、2018 年 1,232、2020 年 512、2022 年 525。

open_tasks.prompt: A news headline says: “Reading your genome now costs less than a new phone, so genetic medicine is here for everyone.” Based on the passage and the chart, write 1–2 English sentences explaining whether this headline tells the whole story.
reference_answers: Not completely, because the chart leaves out the cost of making sense of the data, and new discoveries usually take many years to become part of everyday care.
The cost of sequencing has fallen sharply, but the headline ignores that understanding a genome and using it wisely in medicine are still the harder tasks.
checklist_zh: 有沒有承認成本確實大幅下降
有沒有指出至少一個標題忽略的地方（未含解讀費用、轉成日常醫療需要時間）
理由是否來自文章或圖表
